# ONC - Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT

> ONC leads federal health IT policy, interoperability standards, and certification programs to enable secure nationwide health information exchange.

healthit.gov is the official resource for the Office of the National Coordinator (ONC) under the Assistant Secretary for Technology Policy. It provides comprehensive guidance on health IT certification, interoperability frameworks like TEFCA, data standards including USCDI and FHIR, and sector-specific implementations across behavioral health, emergency services, long-term care, and public health.

## Key Topics

- TEFCA (Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement)
- USCDI (United States Core Data Interoperability)
- FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources)
- Health IT Certification Program
- Information Blocking (21st Century Cures Act)
- Electronic Health Records (EHR)
- Health Information Exchange
- HL7 Standards
- Clinical Quality and Safety
- SAFER Guides
- HITAC (Health Information Technology Advisory Committee)
- Data Interoperability
- Provider Burden Reduction
- USCDI+ (Public Health Extension)

## Interoperability & Exchange Framework

- [Interoperability](https://healthit.gov/interoperability): Health IT interoperability essentials including TEFCA, USCDI, FHIR, and information blocking.
- [TEFCA - Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement](https://healthit.gov/policy/tefca): Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement enabling secure nationwide health information exchange.
- [TEFCA (Detailed Framework)](https://healthit.gov/interoperability/trusted-exchange-framework-and-common-agreement-tefca): TEFCA framework for secure health information exchange among providers, payers, and public health.
- [Information Blocking](https://healthit.gov/information-blocking): 21st Century Cures Act information blocking policies, exceptions, and enforcement under 45 CFR Part 171.

## Health IT Certification & Standards

- [Certification of Health IT](https://healthit.gov/certification-health-it): ONC Health IT Certification Program covering functionality, security, and compliance requirements.
- [Standards & Technology](https://healthit.gov/standards-and-technology): ONC standards and technology including SVAP, USCDI, USCDI Plus, and FHIR specifications.

## Clinical Quality, Safety & Usability

- [Clinical Quality and Safety](https://healthit.gov/clinical-quality-and-safety): Health IT for clinical quality with SAFER Guides, eCQMs, and clinical decision support tools.
- [Usability and Provider Burden](https://healthit.gov/usability-and-provider-burden): EHR usability and provider burden reduction through SAFER Guides and Cures Act certification.

## Sector-Specific Health IT Implementation

- [Public Health](https://healthit.gov/public-health): Health IT for public health with USCDI+ and TEFCA standards for disease prevention and data exchange.
- [Behavioral Health](https://healthit.gov/behavioral-health): Health IT integration for behavioral health care with improved data exchange and patient privacy.
- [Long-Term and Post-Acute Care](https://healthit.gov/long-term-and-post-acute-care): Health IT for long-term and post-acute care with IMPACT Act standards and data exchange.
- [Emergency Medical Services](https://healthit.gov/emergency-medical-services): EMS health IT and NEMSIS data standards for emergency preparedness and patient care records.
- [Pharmacy and Prescription Drug Monitoring Programs](https://healthit.gov/pharmacy-pdmp): PDMP integration with EHRs for opioid prescribing practices and substance use disorder prevention.
- [Maternal and Pediatric Care](https://healthit.gov/maternal-and-pediatric-care): Maternal and pediatric care health IT resources with interoperability best practices and USCDI.

## Policy & Governance

- [HITAC - Health Information Technology Advisory Committee](https://healthit.gov/hitac): Health Information Technology Advisory Committee guiding health IT evolution and policy recommendations.
- [Artificial Intelligence (AI) at HHS](https://healthit.gov/artificial-intelligence): HHS AI and machine learning applications for health outcomes with ethical, effective solutions.
- [Investments](https://healthit.gov/investments): ONC strategic investments in health IT interoperability, Inferno, and Lantern projects.

## Core Resources

- [ONC - Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT](https://healthit.gov): ONC homepage covering health IT interoperability, information sharing, and standardization priorities.
